terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js starts your API on a free port and sends it a few requests.

tasks.title: Create the app and its health check
tasks.description:
Implement `createApp({ store })` in `src/app.js`. It builds a new Express app, adds one route and returns the app **without** calling `listen()`:

- `GET /health` answers `200` with `{ "status": "ok" }` as JSON

Leave the `store` for the next task. `server.js` and `try.js` call `listen()` on the app you return.

The check calls your `createApp`, starts the app on a free port and sends it real requests.
nextSteps: Make a new app with the `express` function you already import.
Return the app at the end of `createApp`.
Run `node try.js` and look at the first answer.
hints: An Express app is made by calling `express()`. Nothing listens until someone calls `listen()` on it.
`app.get(path, handler)` adds a route. The handler gets `req` and `res`, and `res.json(value)` sends a value as JSON with a 200.

videos.title: A REST API with Express in 100 seconds

tasks.title: List the workshops
tasks.description:
Add a second route to `createApp`:

- `GET /workshops` answers `200` with every workshop from `store.list()`, unchanged

Use the `store` that `createApp` is given, not the `workshops` array directly. The check passes a store with workshops of its own, so it can tell the difference. A query string, as in `GET /workshops?day=thu`, must still reach this route.

The check starts your app on a free port and sends it real requests.
nextSteps: Add a route for `GET /workshops` next to the health check.
Answer with what the store lists.
Run `node try.js` and look at the second answer.
hints: The store is already written. Its `list()` gives back an array of workshops.
Express matches routes on the path only, so the query string takes no work from you.

tasks.title: Answer JSON for every other path
tasks.description:
Right now a path with no route gets the HTML page Express sends by itself. The sign-up page reads JSON, so make every other request answer:

- status `404`
- body `{ "error": { "code": "not_found", "message": "..." } }`, where the message is a short sentence for a developer

That includes a known path with a method it has no route for, such as `POST /health`. The routes you already wrote must keep working.

The check sends requests to paths and methods your app does not serve, then one to a route it does.
nextSteps: Run `node try.js` and look at what `/kilns` gets today.
Add a middleware with no path that answers every request that reaches it.
Set the status before you send the JSON.
Think about where it has to go among your routes, then run `node try.js` again.
hints: Express tries routes and middleware in the order you add them. A request that nothing answered falls off the end.
`app.use(handler)` with no path runs for every request that gets that far. Put it after all your routes.
`app.use((req, res) => res.status(404).json({ error: { code: 'not_found', message: ... } }))`, added last.
